title: Agent Pulse
description: One daily evidence-backed decision brief from the coding-agent projects monitored by The Git Reporter.

scope.coverageStatement: V0.2 reports one dated decision brief from direct public source evidence and keeps git motion as a secondary measurement layer. Community feedback metrics are absent until a reproducible feedback collector ships.

inputs.dailyInsight: reported, date-owned Agent Pulse decision brief

editorialRead.headline: Morning Read — October 12, 2026
editorialRead.readHeadline: NousResearch/hermes-agent is the first source to inspect.
editorialRead.oneLineSummary: NousResearch/hermes-agent leads a 3-item attention queue backed by direct receipts; 29 watchlist sources are fresh, 0 need source-health attention, and movement still requires editorial judgment.
editorialRead.dek: Agent Pulse filtered 29 included projects down to 3 items worth finite newsroom attention. The queue protects attention; it does not declare winners.
bullets: NousResearch/hermes-agent — 11 commits today and 1 same-day mapped article, 553.1 below its current daily pace, with 23 hardening-subject points. Inspect the receipt before assigning a story.
openclaw/openclaw — 118 commits landed today. Keep it on watch, but require the next receipt to prove a reader consequence before promoting it.
different-ai/openwork — No same-day commit after 144 commits in the seven-day window. The pause is notable enough to preserve, not enough to turn into a story.
editorialRead.watchNext: The next meaningful upgrade is feedback flow: issues opened and closed, review latency, stale backlog, and the share of work that starts outside the maintainer team.
editorialRead.caveat: Source-code motion and article coverage are collected. GitHub issue flow, PR review timing, community discussion, and private backlog signals are not.

dailyInsight.headline: Read the assembled instructions beside the Hermes code change
dailyInsight.insight: Hermes added committed prompt and tool-schema snapshots for nine controlled configurations. A later named-account snapshot shows the new fields and the instructions a model receives together.
dailyInsight.mechanism: The production assembler renders a fixed development matrix. A staleness test compares regenerated output with committed files, while an advisory summary and a separate designated-team review rule expose changes for human judgment.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: A reviewer can inspect the instructions produced by code instead of reconstructing their combined effect from implementation edits.

actions.audience: Hermes contributors and maintainers reviewing instruction changes
actions.label: Compare one rendered schema change with its implementation
actions.instruction: Open the October 11 named-account snapshot and its connection-tool changes. Check that account naming, repair and rename parameters agree with the prose. Use the full committed schema diff as well as the summary, and test the relevant behavior separately.
actions.effort: One focused source review; no deployment change

receipts.title: Rendered prompt and tool-schema review baseline
receipts.supports: Nine selected configurations, committed output and staleness checking.

receipts.title: Named-account snapshot exposes parameters and instruction prose
receipts.supports: Concrete schema and account-naming instruction update in the new review artifact.

confidence.basis: Inspected pinned implementation, prior docs, actual schema update and active public review rule; isolated upstream summary test passed.

dailyInsight.limitation: The nine configurations omit user-specific context and later runtime inputs. The full renderer and model behavior were not tested; neither snapshot consistency nor approval establishes task success. Latest inspected stable release predates the change.
dailyInsight.falsifier: A reproducible default prompt or tool-schema change in a covered configuration that fails to alter the rendered snapshot would weaken the review-coverage finding.
dailyInsight.watchNext: A public PR where a rendered difference leads to an instruction correction and a behavior test.
